$docs.purpose: Structural bundle budgets enforced by scripts/check-bundle-budgets.mjs. Every emitted JS/CSS byte must be classified and budgeted; every rule here is a reviewable diff.
$docs.compression: All sizes are brotli (quality 11), matching `npm run size-limit`.

initialLoad.entryJsLimitKb: Brotli size of the HTML entry chunk(s) alone (app code, no vendor).
initialLoad.totalJsLimitKb: Brotli size of everything downloaded before first paint: entry chunk(s) plus every chunk statically reachable from them. Lazy chunks never count toward this, so moving code into a lazily-loaded chunk cannot hide it here — but lazy routes are pinned by `lazyRoutes` below.
initialLoad.cssLimitKb: Brotli size of CSS referenced by the initial chunks.

vendorChunks.semantics: Key = Rollup manualChunks name. `packages` is an exact allowlist of npm packages allowed inside the chunk (verified from the build's module map, not chunk names). A new dependency, transitive or not, must be added here explicitly. `mustBeLazy: true` fails the build if the chunk becomes statically reachable from the entry.

lazyRoutes.semantics: Exact allowlist of dynamic route entries (manifest keys). A dynamic import for anything not listed fails CI, so `lazy()` can no longer be used to dodge the initial-load budget. `chunkLimitKb` budgets the route's own chunk; `subtreeLimitKb` budgets everything non-initial it pulls in (vendor chunks included).

invariants: Coverage: every emitted JS/CSS file must be classified (initial, vendor, or claimed by a lazy route) — no orphan chunks.
Initial-load boundary: initial download = entry + statically reachable vendor chunks only; the lazy-route set is closed under this config.
Vendor attribution: each vendor chunk is budgeted and its npm packages are verified against the allowlist.
